shortDescription: The German baseload contract for Monday delivery jumped over €200 on Friday as lower renewable output was expected, piling additional upward pressure on a country already facing high gas costs.($1 = 0.8617 euros)

children: The German baseload contract for Monday delivery jumped over €200 on Friday as lower renewable output was expected, piling additional upward pressure on a country already facing high gas costs.
The German Monday baseload contract (TRDEBD3) was at €223 ($258.79) per megawatt-hour at 0747 GMT, LSEG data showed.
Both wind and solar power supply are expected to drop on Monday by 3.1 gigawatts and 1.4 GW, respectively, driving up the need for gas-fired power supply to fill the gap, LSEG data showed.
Spot prices rise sharply in the evening, mainly reflecting the strong increase in gas prices in recent weeks and their impact on marginal generation costs, EnergyScan analysts said.
Wind generation should rise next week, providing some relief to spot power prices, they added.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD3) was untraded early, according to LSEG data.
French renewable supply is flat, with wind supply expected down 630 megawatts and solar supply seen up by 390 MW, while slightly lower demand offsets any gains in residual load, LSEG data showed.
French nuclear availability fell by four percentage points, to 70% of total capacity as the Flamanville 1 reactor went offline for planned maintenance.
On the forward side, the German year-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) retreated early by 0.3% to €132.89/MWh after a week of gains, the data showed.

Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha on Thursday and advanced down the Red Sea coast to strategic islands, gaining further leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, military sources said.
The strait is the southern outlet of the Red Sea and one of the world's most important shipping routes for gas and oil.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) had a bid-ask range between €89/MWh and €94/MWh, LSEG data showed.
